findings.body:
**Remove the head-owned `.gitleaksignore` before scanning.**

A PR can add a detected secret and put its finding fingerprint in `.gitleaksignore`. Gitleaks v8.30.1 loads that file from the scanned checkout and suppresses the finding despite the trusted `--config`. Clean commit messages then leave the required check green. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/v8.30.1/cmd/root.go))

Remove or replace the head-owned ignore file before all scans. Setting `--gitleaks-ignore-path` alone is insufficient: this version also loads the source-directory `.gitleaksignore`. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/v8.30.1/cmd/root.go))

Apply the fix in the template and re-instantiate. As per path instructions, “Workflow edits route through policy/templates/ re-instantiation”.
findings.title: Remove the head-owned `.gitleaksignore` before scanning.

findings.body:
**Disable head-controlled inline suppressions.**

If a commit message contains a detected secret and `gitleaks:allow` on the same line, Gitleaks v8.30.1 suppresses the finding by default. The trusted TOML does not prevent this bypass. The two diff scans use the same default. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/v8.30.1/cmd/root.go))

Add `--ignore-gitleaks-allow` to all three invocations. This prevents scanned content from overriding the trusted policy and is separate from ignore-file loading. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/v8.30.1/cmd/root.go))

Apply the fix in the template and re-instantiate. As per path instructions, “Workflow edits route through policy/templates/ re-instantiation”.
findings.title: Disable head-controlled inline suppressions.
